notes: Read all 86 source lines before editing. This is pure, framework-agnostic TypeScript (Date arithmetic, Number.isFinite, Array push/sort) with no DOM, browser, Recharts, Leaflet, or web-UI dependency, so the windowing logic ports verbatim and runs identically under Hermes/JSC.

L1 import: web pulls `FSMTransition` from the `@/types/fsm` alias which does not exist in the native workspace; remapped to `import type { FSMTransition } from '../../../../api/hooks/useFSM'` — the structurally identical DTO (id, vehicle_id, ts, fsm_name, from_state, to_state, trigger, details?) already inlined by the native useFSM hook, same precedent as sibling FSMHealthPanel.tsx. `import type` is erased at compile time, so no runtime coupling is added.
L3-13 module JSDoc preserved verbatim (intent: single source of truth for windowing FSM transitions; reconciles the page 'buffered' counter and StateTimeline tick filter to one scope).

L15-26 WindowedTransitions interface ported verbatim: inWindow, outsideWindow, lastTransition (FSMTransition | null), anchor (Date), minutes — all field names, optionality, and per-field doc comments preserved.

L28-35 PRESETS_MIN `[5, 10, 30, 120, 360, 1440] as const` preserved exactly, including the JSDoc explaining the toolbar exposes the [5,10,30,120] subset while the helper additionally considers [360,1440].

L37-67 windowTransitions() ported byte-for-byte: anchor default `?? new Date()`, endTs/startTs window math with `minutes * 60_000`, the -Infinity/last-transition scan, `Number.isFinite(ts)` skip guard, inclusive [startTs,endTs] bucket test, and ascending sort of both buckets by `new Date(ts).getTime()`. No unit-suffixed fields touched; all values are minutes/milliseconds time math, not SI distance/speed/energy quantities, so the Phase-48 SI canonical rules do not apply. No i18n strings, no API paths, no visual surface in this file.
